title: High cholesterol: what to cut down and what to add
intro: When the doctor says your cholesterol is high, many people immediately think they have to eat bland food. Actually, it doesn't have to be that way. You can start by cutting down a few things and adding a few others. You can still eat your favourite food, just less often and in smaller portions. This helps together with the treatment your doctor gives.

sections.p: Cut down on saturated fat and fried food. For example, thick santan (coconut milk), chicken skin, fatty meat, tripe, butter, ghee and battered fried food. Biscuits, cakes and pastries are also often high in fat. No need to cut them out completely. Make them once-in-a-while food.

Add high-fibre food like oats, dhal, red beans, vegetables and fruit. This type of fibre can help your body manage cholesterol. Also add fish like kembung, sardines and tenggiri, at least twice a week. A small handful of unsalted nuts can also be a snack.

Choose steaming, boiling, baking, grilling or stir-frying with a little oil. For masak lemak or curry, try using thin santan or half santan, mixed with low-fat milk. Remove chicken skin before cooking. Drain off excess oil.

At the mamak, choose roti kosong or chapati instead of roti telur bawang or murtabak. At nasi campur, take grilled dishes or soup and more vegetables. Ask for just a little kuah (gravy). Nasi lemak is okay once in a while, for example with a boiled egg and cucumber.

Walking comfortably every day can help heart health. Chair exercises and wall push-ups are suitable for sensitive knees. Start slowly, for example 10 minutes, and add more once your body gets used to it.

action: Remove chicken skin and fat from meat before cooking or eating.
Change one fried dish a week to grilled, steamed or soup.
Eat fish like kembung or sardines twice a week.
Add one serving of fruit and one serving of vegetables every day.
Walk 10 to 20 minutes a day, as much as you can manage.
doctor: See your doctor first before starting exercise if you have heart disease, have had a stroke, or have uncontrolled diabetes or high blood pressure. Get urgent treatment if you feel pain or tightness in your chest, pain spreading to your arm or jaw, shortness of breath or weakness on one side of the body. If you take cholesterol medicine, don't change or stop it on your own, even if your readings have come down. Discuss with your doctor.

faq.a: For most people, eggs can be eaten in moderate amounts. Boiled or steamed is better than fried in lots of oil. Ask your doctor how many are suitable for your condition.

faq.q: Can't I eat prawns and squid at all?
faq.a: You can have them once in a while in normal portions. How they're cooked matters more, for example grilled squid is better than battered fried squid. Follow your doctor's advice if your readings are very high.

faq.q: If I'm already on medicine, do I still need to watch what I eat?
faq.a: Yes, watching what you eat and staying active are still important alongside medicine. Both help each other. Keep taking your medicine as your doctor instructs and discuss if you have any questions.
